CVE-2026-115683.title: epiphany: TLS certificate warning bypass via race in tlsErrorPage message handler
CVE-2026-115683.description:
A race condition in Epiphany allows a malicious website to bypass the TLS/SSL certificate warning page.

Epiphany registers the main-world script message handler "tlsErrorPage" so its internal TLS error page can implement "Accept Risk and Proceed". The handler was registered immediately before loading the error page, leaving a brief window where the previously loaded untrusted origin could still call window.webkit.messageHandlers.tlsErrorPage.postMessage(...). The only authorization check compares a numeric WebKit page id that increments predictably; an attacker can burst-guess ids and approve a certificate exception with no user click.

If a victim visits malicious site A that redirects to site B with an invalid certificate, site A can, for a few milliseconds, disable TLS certificate error warnings for host B until Epiphany is restarted, enabling man-in-the-middle or site spoofing for that host.

Upstream report: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/work_items/2978
Proof of…

CVE-2026-116242.title: pgAdmin 4: SSH tunnels use the pgAdmin service account's own SSH identity
CVE-2026-116242.description:
pgAdmin 4 opens SSH tunnels with the sshtunnel library but gave it neither host_pkey_directories nor ssh_config_file, so it always loaded the unencrypted private keys in ~/.ssh of the operating-system account running pgAdmin, read that account's ~/.ssh/config (IdentityFile, User, HostName, ProxyCommand) for the tunnel host, and could use its ssh-agent. In server mode any user could therefore configure a tunnel to a host that accepts the service account's key, with no credentials of their own or with an identity file that did not exist in their storage, and reach it as that account.

The fix makes tunnels in server mode use only the identity file or password the user configured: the service account's keys, configuration and agent are no longer used, and an identity file that cannot be found in the user's storage is reported instead of falling back to ~/.ssh. Desktop mode is unchanged.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

CVE-2026-132275.title: svglib: Exponential resource consumption via nested <use> references in svg2rlg
CVE-2026-132275.description: svglib reads SVG files and converts them to other formats. Prior to 2.3.1, the svg2rlg() renderer recursively expands nested SVG <use> references by deep-copying each referenced subtree; SvgRenderer.renderUse() in src/svglib/svglib.py calls xlink_href_target(), which rejects direct cycles but permits acyclic reference graphs with repeated fan-out. A small attacker-controlled SVG can therefore trigger exponentially increasing node expansion, consuming excessive CPU and memory in any application that renders it without a non-default option; HTML-to-PDF workflows using xhtml2pdf can reach the same renderer when an embedded data:image/svg+xml image in an HTML img element is passed to pisa.CreatePDF(). This issue is fixed in 2.3.1.

CVE-2026-133188.title: MISP Protected Event Signature Bypass via Whitespace Injection in JSON Keys and Identifiers
CVE-2026-133188.description:
MISP contains a vulnerability in the cryptographic signature verification of protected events. When a MISP instance signs a protected event for synchronization, it strips all whitespace from the JSON body before computing the PGP signature (preg_replace("/\s+/", "", $data)). The receiving instance performs the same whitespace-stripping before verification. Because the signature covers only the whitespace-free representation, a network relay positioned between two MISP instances can insert whitespace characters into JSON object keys (effectively renaming fields) or into identifier values such as UUIDs, timestamps, and distribution fields without invalidating the signature. The receiving instance accepts the modified event as authentic.

CVE-2026-133838.description:
FlowIntel contains an authorization bypass that allows non-approver case members to modify restricted tasks (those in Requested, Rejected, or Request Review status) through several indirect code paths that lacked the required approver permission check.

Affected operations include:
- Self-unassignment from a restricted task
- Reordering tasks, including indirectly moving restricted sibling tasks
- Linking or unlinking MISP objects and attributes to/from restricted tasks
- Creating MISP objects or standalone attributes with task IDs referencing restricted tasks
- Deleting MISP objects or attributes that are linked to restricted tasks
- Executing modules on restricted tasks

A user with case member access (but without Admin, Case Admin, or Queue Admin privileges) could exploit these paths to alter the state of tasks that are supposed to be locked pending approval, effectively bypassing the intended approval workflow and potentially manipulating associated MISP data.

CVE-2026-55505.title: Wavelog: Authenticated SSRF-to-Local-File-Read via LotW Import file:// Scheme
CVE-2026-55505.description: Wavelog is web-based amateur radio logging software. A standard user can trigger the LotW import, although changing lotw_download_url normally requires installer administrator access, and related vulnerabilities can remove that prerequisite. The same missing status-validation pattern affects the LotW lotw_users fetch helper and per-user download helper. This exposes files readable by the www-data user, including environment data, mounted secrets, and application configuration. This issue is fixed in version 3.2.4.

CVE-2026-99358.title: nfsd: zero NFSv4 COMPOUND tag padding
CVE-2026-99358.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: zero NFSv4 COMPOUND tag padding

nfs4svc_encode_compoundres() copies the tag bytes into reserved XDR space
and skips directly to the aligned end of the field. xdr_reserve_space()
rounds the reservation up but does not initialize the padding bytes.

A remote client can choose a tag length that is not a multiple of four,
causing one to three stale bytes from the response page to be returned in
the COMPOUND reply.

Use xdr_encode_opaque_fixed() to copy the tag and clear its XDR padding.
